issues.legal_issue: The residence of a Hindu undivided family depends on where the controlling and directive power over its income-related affairs functions with some permanence, rather than on isolated activity.
material_facts: The family’s karta lived abroad with his family and carried on business there.
The family had property, investments, and business interests in India.
During visits to India, the karta attended to family litigation and tax proceedings and started two partnership businesses.
issues.conclusion: The karta’s visits, attendance to family matters, and business activity in India did not by themselves establish that the family’s control and management was situated in India or that it had a second centre of control there.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 4A(b) of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, control and management means the controlling and directive power—the ‘head and brain’ of the affairs—and ‘situated’ requires that power to function at a place with some degree of permanence. ‘Affairs’ means affairs relevant to income under the Act. Mere activity in a place does not establish residence there; control may be divided between places, and a Hindu undivided family may accordingly have more than one residence. The Court relied on De Beers v. Howe and Swedish Central Railway Co. Ltd. v. Thompson.

predicates.hindu_family_tax_residence_case: The proceeding determines the tax residence of a Hindu undivided family.
predicates.control_wholly_outside_taxable_territory: The family’s controlling and directive power over its income-related affairs functions wholly outside the taxable territory with some degree of permanence.

issues.definition: When a tax-residence proceeding concerns a Hindu undivided family and its controlling and directive power functions wholly outside the taxable territory with some degree of permanence, the family is not resident there.

issues.legal_issue: An assessee claiming that a Hindu undivided family’s control and management is wholly outside the taxable territory bears the burden of proving that claim, and the ordinary residence presumption applies if the burden is not discharged.
material_facts: The karta lived abroad, but the family had affairs and business interests in India.
The karta attended to litigation concerning family property and to tax proceedings during his visits to India, and started two businesses in India.
The assessee did not produce correspondence or other material that could show that the Indian affairs were normally controlled from abroad.
The evidence did not establish that control and management of the family’s affairs was wholly outside India.
issues.conclusion: The assessee did not discharge the burden of proving that the family’s control and management was wholly outside the taxable territory, so the ordinary presumption applied and the family was treated as resident for the assessment year in issue. The decision was confined to that year, and the assessee could seek to establish the contrary for later years with proper evidence.
issues.legal_principle: Section 4A(b) of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, ordinarily treats a Hindu undivided family as resident in the taxable territories unless the control and management of its affairs is situated wholly outside them. The assessee bears the burden of proving facts bringing the case within that exception. Relevant acts in the taxable territory may not be conclusive of a local centre of control, but they are not irrelevant; failure to produce material evidence that would show the affairs were normally controlled from outside permits the ordinary presumption to apply.

rule.if: hindu_family_tax_residence_case and indian_income_related_affairs_exist and karta_performs_relevant_acts_in_territory and evidence_of_normal_foreign_control_not_produced

predicates.hindu_family_tax_residence_case: The proceeding determines the tax residence of a Hindu undivided family.
predicates.indian_income_related_affairs_exist: The family has affairs in the territory that are relevant to income taxation.
predicates.karta_performs_relevant_acts_in_territor: The family’s karta attends to family or tax matters, or undertakes business activity, in the territory.
predicates.evidence_of_normal_foreign_control_not_p: The assessee does not produce material evidence showing that the family’s affairs in the territory are normally controlled from outside it.

issues.definition: In a Hindu-family tax-residence proceeding, where income-related affairs exist in the territory, the karta performs relevant acts there, and evidence of normal control from outside is not produced, the family is treated as resident in the territory.
